summary: Georgian Bay range lights of 1894 that lead ships into Parry Sound. The rear tower is a federal heritage building, and the Coast Guard plans to demolish it.

light.range_note: Canadian Coast Guard list (rear). The register gives 8 nautical miles for the rear light; see notes.

structures.note: Red and white tower on a hipped-roof dwelling, Jones Island.
On the summit of Gordon Rock; focal height 12.4 m, nominal range 10 nm (CCG list).

staffing.note: Last head keeper named by LighthouseFriends: Joseph G. Dixon, 1917 to 1919. No source here dates the end of resident keeping.

access.note: Owned by the Canadian Coast Guard. Grounds and tower closed; best seen by boat.

events.note: Built by contract (Mickler), finished by the Department's foreman of works after defects were found (LighthouseFriends; register).
Placed in operation 29 September 1894 (LighthouseFriends). The Department's 1900 table gives 25 July 1894 for a range keeper's appointment; not used.
Steamer Arthur Orr struck a shoal entering Parry Sound on the range, 3 May 1901. A pinnacle 450 ft NE of the range was found and buoyed.
Range lights painted white throughout for the opening of navigation in 1902.
Front light changed from fixed red to fixed white, 7 June 1915 (LighthouseFriends).
Rear light fitted with a duplex lamp and a 25-inch long-focus reflector, 24 August 1915 (LighthouseFriends).
Recognized as a Federal Heritage Building on 27 March 2008 (register entry 21066).
Coast Guard letter to Carling Township, 9 July 2025, reports extensive structural deterioration and plans demolition and an 80-foot replacement tower about 15 m away (Parry Sound North Star).

keepers.name: Thomas W. Huff
keepers.note: Born Yorkville (Toronto) 1845; settled in Parry Sound 1865; jeweller, watchmaker and gunsmith in 1894. $400 a year; also expected to keep the Hugh Rock light. A Parry Sound complaint about lights not regularly lit (relayed from the Red Rock keeper) was made soon after opening. LighthouseFriends says he stayed through 1900.

corrections.why: The record's coordinates are those of the front light on Gordon Rock (CCG: 45 18 55.8 N, 80 16 56.7 W). The rear light is at CCG 45 17 57.8 N, 80 15 24.8 W, and LighthouseFriends gives 45.29952, -80.256988 for it.
12.4 m is the focal height of the front light; the rear light's is 18.7 m (CCG list).
10 nm is the front light's nominal range; the CCG list gives the rear light 17 nm. The register gives 8 nm for the rear light, so the sources disagree.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard list gives nominal ranges of 10 nm (front) and 17 nm (rear). The Parks register gives 7 nm (front) and 8 nm (rear). The sources are not reconciled here; the official list is used in the record.

notes_for_editor: Record errors: the coordinates, focal height and range in this record are the front light's; corrections are proposed above. Range: the Coast Guard list gives nominal ranges of 10 nm (front) and 17 nm (rear); the register gives 7 nm (front) and 8 nm (rear). Not reconciled; the story says so. Operating status: the Coast Guard list marks both range lights 'Operates 24 h.' and 'Seasonal (in place year round)'. The story reports both remarks. Rear tower position: the register says the north-east tip; LighthouseFriends says near the southern end and, quoting an older Department description, the south-west point. The story gives these as disagreement. Huff: LighthouseFriends' text says he stayed keeper through 1900; its keeper list runs him to 1901. The story gives both. The complaint about Gordon Rock and Hugh Rock lights is paraphrased; the earlier draft wrongly put LighthouseFriends' paraphrase in quotation marks as Lawson's words. 1901 Arthur Orr: the 3 May sentence sits on the page before the 450-foot placement (scan 68, printed 53?) and the placement and master's remark on scan 69 (printed 54). The footnote now cites both scans. The pinnacle (found and buoyed) is at scan 58 (printed page not confirmed). The Black Rock beacon blown down in September 1901 (scan 68) is a different light on the same approach and is used only as context. 1909 'Ed. Taylor' line: one OCR line carries name, station and salary together; read from the text and not checked on the page image (scan 177). Keeper gap 1910-1916 unchanged. Parry Sound North Star article: undated in the cached copy; it cites an Archipelago Township council agenda dated 20 February, so it is from early 2026. The Coast Guard's plans and status may have changed since. Lis McWalter is named as a public advocate quoted in the newspaper. Do not confuse with the Jones Island Range on the Ottawa River (Carillon Island, Quebec, 1908), which has its own Department entries and keepers. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts paraphrased and quotations limited. Wikipedia not used.
